facts.raw_span: A 27-year-old man
history of a 5 mm‐thick melanoma on his posterior neck
treated six years earlier by wide local excision
no sentinel lymph node biopsy, no adjuvant therapy
presented with hemoptysis and dyspnea
Vital signs were within normal limits
Physical examination was notable only for scattered breath sounds without stridor
Contrast-enhanced CT of the chest revealed a 3.1 × 2.7 × 3.6 cm mass in the right lower lobe
Endobronchial ultrasound–guided fine-needle aspiration of the lung lesion demonstrated a malignant small round blue cell tumor
Molecular studies were negative for an EWSR1 translocation but otherwise were interpreted as consistent with Ewing sarcoma/primitive neuroectodermal tumor (PNET)
Positron emission tomography (PET)/CT showed an FDG-avid right lower lobe mass
an intensely FDG-avid, partially calcified 4.1 × 2.3 × 2.8 cm expansile lesion within the right hyoid bone

rationales.F02: History of melanoma increases the likelihood of metastatic melanoma.
rationales.F08: A mass in the right lower lobe is consistent with Ewing sarcoma or PNET.
rationales.F09: Malignant small round blue cell tumor is consistent with Ewing sarcoma or PNET.
rationales.F10: Molecular studies consistent with Ewing sarcoma/PNET rule in these diagnoses.
rationales.F12: An expansile lesion in the hyoid bone could be a primary bone tumor such as plasmacytoma, chondrosarcoma, or osteosarcoma.

frontier_selector.why: The evidence from endobronchial ultrasound–guided fine-needle aspiration and molecular studies specifically supports Ewing sarcoma over other options.
